source.description:
## PROBLEM
service-skills v2 (epic xtrm-b86y5) gives a repo a registry of per-service expert skills + a
generated per-repo umbrella (`<repo>-services`). Claude Code consumes them via hooks
(SessionStart catalog, PreToolUse activator). **Specialists do not** — an executor/debugger/
reviewer working in a repo with a populated service-registry gets none of that operational
context auto-injected. Should they? And if so, which ones, and how much?

## OPEN DESIGN QUESTION (evaluate first — this is a decision bead)
**Does every specialist need service-skills detail injected, or only some?**
- Probably NOT uniform: editors that touch service code (executor, debugger) benefit most;
  read-only/meta roles (reviewer, code-sanity, obligations-scanner, planner, sync-docs) may
  not — injection is token cost for little gain, and reviewer audits against the bead, not ambient context.
- Granularity: inject the **umbrella** (cheap, ~1 skill, whole-repo map) vs the **specific
  per-service skill(s)** matched to the bead's SCOPE territory (richer, but needs territory→service
  resolution at dispatch) vs **nothing unless asked**.
- Trigger: only when a registry is present (registry-gated, no-op otherwise) — that's the
  "when the registry is present maybe" the operator flagged.

## CANDIDATE MECHANISMS (to compare, not yet chosen)
1. **Specialist `skills.paths` entry** pointing at the active `service-skills` umbrella —
   simplest, static, every run of that specialist loads the umbrella. (Cheap, coarse.)
2. **Pre-script injector** (like service-skills-sync already uses `drift_detector scan` as a
   pre-script): a registry-gated pre-script that resolves the bead's SCOPE → owning service(s)
   via bootstrap `find_service_for_path` + gitnexus, and injects only those service skills.
   (Targeted, but adds dispatch-time work.)
2b. A small **specialists extension** that, on run, detects a service-registry and injects the
    umbrella + territory-matched services into context. (The operator's "extension" idea.)
3. **Per-role policy**: a capability flag on the specialist definition
   (`consumes_service_skills: umbrella|matched|none`) so each role opts in at the right depth.

## SUCCESS (of the eventual decision + impl)
A documented decision on (a) which specialist roles consume service-skills, (b) at what
granularity (umbrella vs matched vs none), (c) the mechanism, and (d) the registry-gating —
plus, if green-lit, the implementation. Specialists in service-registry repos get the right
operational context without blanket token bloat.

## SCOPE
specialists repo (specialist definitions, runner/pre-script or extension surface, skills.paths);
xtrm-tools service-skills bootstrap resolvers (find_service_for_path, get_umbrella_dir) as the
territory→service + umbrella-locate primitives the injector would call.

## NON_GOALS
- Not changing the Claude-Code hook path (already works).
- Not forcing injection on read-only/meta roles before the cost/benefit is evaluated.
- No new service-skill content model change.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Registry-gated: zero behavior change in repos without a service-registry.
- Respect token budget — measure injection cost per role; reviewer-style roles default off.
- Reuse v2 resolvers (bootstrap.find_service_for_path / get_umbrella_dir / get_service_skill_path_str);
  don't reinvent territory→service matching.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Decision recorded: role→granularity matrix + mechanism choice + gating
- [ ] (if impl) a service-registry repo shows the chosen specialist(s) receiving umbrella/matched context; non-registry repos unchanged
- [ ] token-cost measurement per role captured to justify the matrix

## OUTPUT
A decision record (matrix + mechanism + rationale) and, if approved, the extension/pre-script/
skills.paths implementation + tests.

## REFERENCES
- Builds on epic xtrm-b86y5 (Service Skills v2). Real-world migration under test via
  mercury-market-data-7x0d. Existing precedent: service-skills-sync.specialist.json already
  uses a drift_detector pre-script + skills.paths — a model for option 1/2.
source.title: Design: specialists consuming service-skills when a registry is present
